excerpt: Mixhalo streams live-event audio and real-time translation to attendees' phones with no extra hardware. DeepL acquired Mixhalo in June 2026.
content:
Mixhalo is a San Francisco audio technology company. It takes sound straight from a venue's mixing desk and streams it with very low delay to attendees' smartphones, so people can listen through their own headphones. Its website describes it as an AI-enabled digital audio platform for live events with a zero-hardware approach, used for "silent" sessions, live interpretation, transcription and summaries. Mixhalo Translate delivers real-time translated audio and captions for conferences, where speakers and audiences often do not share a language. TechCrunch reported that Mixhalo started out improving concert sound and later moved into sports and live events, with its technology used at Metallica and Sting shows as well as MLB and NASCAR events.

Mixhalo was founded in 2016 by Incubus guitarist Mike Einziger, violinist Ann Marie Simpson-Einziger and Vik Singh, who is CEO. TechCrunch reported that it raised more than $39 million from investors including Fortress Investment Group, Founders Fund, Defy Partners and Cowboy Ventures.

Acquisition by DeepL

On 17 June 2026 the German translation company DeepL announced it had acquired Mixhalo; terms were not disclosed. DeepL said it would bring Mixhalo's ultra-low-latency audio into DeepL Voice, its real-time voice translation product, so it can work at large live events, and would open a Bay Area office. Mixhalo was already a DeepL customer, using it as its main translation engine. Mixhalo's website now says it is part of DeepL.

Pricing

Mixhalo does not publish prices. Event organisers and venues contact its sales team for a quote.

Who it suits

It suits conference organisers who need live interpretation or silent sessions, and venues, leagues and artists who want to offer better audio to fans. Small meetings may not need a dedicated platform.

We have not used Mixhalo. This page is based on Mixhalo's website and on TechCrunch and Tech.eu coverage of the DeepL deal.
